name: Setwell Blind Dates
need: Can someone just set me up on a real date so I don't have to swipe?
headline: No swiping, no chatting. We pick one compatible person, book the time and place, and you both just show up.
buyer: Single adults (18+, ID-verified) in a metro area, usually 25-45, who have tried the apps and are worn out by them. They want a few good dates and won't pay $4,000+ for a human matchmaker.
bullets: A 15-minute intake (values, dealbreakers, schedule), then a human-reviewed match suggestion each week, sent with a short explanation of why the two of you might fit
Both people opt in before anything is booked. We pick a public venue and a time that suits both calendars, and nobody has to send a single message
After each date both people give private feedback, which tunes the next match. Every profile is ID- and age-verified, and both sides see the same information
priceNote: You only pay for dates that actually get booked. A setup comes back as a credit if the match doesn't confirm. This sits between Sitch ($89.99 for 3 setups) and Tawkify client packages (thousands of dollars).
reasonPrompt: What usually goes wrong for you between matching with someone and actually sitting across from them on a date?

faq.q: Is the other person real and actually interested?
faq.a: Yes. Every member is ID-verified and 18+. Nothing is booked until both people have seen the match and said yes, and we never write messages for anyone or pose as anyone.

faq.q: What if the date is a no-show?
faq.a: If the other person doesn't show, the setup comes back as a credit. Repeat no-shows are removed from the service.

faq.q: How is this different from a dating app?
faq.a: There's no feed, no swiping and no chatting. You get one considered match at a time and a booked plan.
We launch one metro at a time, and only once there are enough verified members on both sides to make good matches.
No. This page checks whether enough people want it. Leave your email and you will hear when it is ready. Nothing is charged.

demand.summary: Pay-per-introduction matchmaking that skips the swiping already has paying customers at several price levels: Sitch sells setup packs and was funded by a16z speedrun and M13, Swoony has verified recurring revenue, and Tawkify has 8,000+ Trustpilot reviews. Users who say they had 'been on all the apps' describe weekly introductions they look forward to and blind dates that work.
demand.wtp: Sitch's in-app purchases: 3 setups $89.99, 5 for $124.99, 8 for $159.99, plus Sitch Monthly at $29.99 (App Pricing Lab, checked 2026-08-10). Swoony on TrustMRR: $45,639 all-time revenue, $1,434 MRR, 49 active subscriptions. Tawkify: TrustScore 4.6 from 8,044 Trustpilot reviews, with client packages that run into the thousands.

signals.quote: I feel special when I get an introduction every week. I wait for it.

signals.quote: A lot of the dating apps behave similarly to mobile games
3 Setups: $89.99 ... 5 setups: $124.99 ... Sitch Monthly: $29.99 ... 8 Setups: $159.99
All-time revenue: $45,639 ... MRR: $1,434 ... Active subscriptions: 49
I had been on all the apps and tried everything.
It was a perfect blind date.

demand.competitors: Sitch (AI and human, pay per setup, NYC/SF/LA), Swoony (AI match suggestions on subscription), Keeper (AI matchmaker, high-end bounty model, per press coverage), Tawkify (human matchmakers, packages in the thousands), Hinge and other swipe apps.
demand.risks: Two-sided supply in each city, and the gender balance inside it. No-shows and safety at first meetings (fix with public venues and ID checks). Sitch already holds this exact position in its cities, so we need a sharper price or more cities. The Swoony revenue on TrustMRR is small, which suggests subscriptions alone convert slowly.

name: Vouchring
need: All my friends are coupled up. How do I get them to actually set me up with someone?
headline: Let the people who know you play matchmaker. Friends vouch for you and suggest you to their single friends, and setups happen only with everyone's consent.
buyer: Single adults (18+) in their late 20s to 40s whose friends are mostly married. Those friends would happily set them up, but they never think of it and have no easy way to do it.
bullets: Invite 3-5 friends to write a short, honest vouch for you, so a potential date sees what your people say about you instead of a cold profile
Your friends (single or coupled) get a private board of single friends-of-friends and can suggest a pairing with one tap. Both singles see who suggested it and why, and each one opts in
Turn an agreed setup into a double date or a group hang with the matchmaker friend, so the first meeting feels low-pressure
price: $12/month for singles; free for matchmaker friends
priceNote: Matchmaking friends never pay, which keeps them suggesting. That's below Loop Premium ($29.99/month) because the network comes from friends instead of strangers.
reasonPrompt: Who are the people in your life who'd set you up if it were easy? What's stopped them so far?

faq.q: Can a friend set me up without my knowing?
faq.a: No. Your profile appears only after you approve each vouch, and a setup happens only when both singles say yes. Every member is ID- and age-verified (18+).

faq.q: Can friends write things about me I don't approve?
faq.a: You see every vouch and choose which ones show. Nothing goes live without your OK.

faq.q: Do my friends need to be single?
faq.a: No. Married and coupled friends are the best matchmakers, and they use it for free.
No. There's no feed of strangers. Every suggestion comes from a real person who knows at least one of you.
No. This page checks whether enough people want it. Leave your email and you will hear when it is ready. Nothing is charged.

demand.summary: People who are tired of the apps say they want to be set up, and that their coupled-up friends don't think to do it. Set-up dates appeal because the other person has 'been vetted already'. Loop, which matches through friends, has 1K ratings and charges for Premium and intro requests, which shows people pay for this.
demand.wtp: Loop Premium, iOS: $29.99 per month, $74.99 for 3 months, $179.99 per year. Premium Intro Requests cost $9.99-$19.99. Rated 4.6 from 1K ratings on the App Store.

signals.quote: most of my single friends are tired of the top dating apps and looking to be set up

signals.quote: 1 Month: $29.99 ... 1 Year: $179.99 (Loop Premium); 4.6 out of 5, 1K ratings
So being set up with someone through them feels like it's not even on their radar.

signals.who: Saskia, set up by a mutual friend (Fashion Journal, Cait Emma Burke)
signals.quote: I was pretty over the dating scene and really wanted love.
The comfortability you get from going on a set up date is knowing that the person has been vetted already.

demand.competitors: Loop (matchmaking through friends and groups, paid Premium), Hinge and Bumble (no friend-vouch layer), Facebook setup groups (informal), and older attempts like Spritzr and YouShouldTotallyMeet that seem to have shut down (snippet only, status not checked).
demand.risks: Cold start: each single has to recruit friends to vouch, and many earlier friend-matchmaking apps faded. Friends' interest may drop after the first week, so prompts and small rewards matter. Privacy, because friends see other people's single friends (mitigate with opt-in visibility). Loop already exists, so the vouch and double-date angle has to set this apart.

name: Tablefor6 Singles
need: Is there a way to meet single people in person without the apps or awkward bar nights?
headline: Dinner for six single strangers, matched by age range and interests, with equal numbers of women and men guaranteed before any table is confirmed.
buyer: Single adults (18+, ID-verified), mostly 25-45, who are 'sick of online dating' and want to meet people face to face. They find speed dating too intense and friendship dinners not aimed at singles.
bullets: Answer a short questionnaire, pick your nights, and get placed at a table of six singles in your age range at a local restaurant
Tables are confirmed only when the gender mix (or same-gender mix for queer tables) is balanced, so you never pay for a lopsided night
Afterward you privately mark who you'd like to see again. Contact details are shared only when it's mutual
price: $29 per month (up to 3 dinners); food and drinks paid at the restaurant
priceNote: In line with Timeleft's US pricing (about $16 per dinner, $26 per month for unlimited) but only for singles, with a guaranteed balance at the table. If your table doesn't confirm, the seat is refunded as a credit.
reasonPrompt: When did you last meet someone you were interested in face to face, and what made it happen?

faq.q: Is this a dating event or a friendship dinner?
faq.a: Everyone at the table is single and open to dating. Whether anything comes of it is up to you. Mutual matches are revealed only after the dinner.

faq.q: What if the ratio is off?
faq.a: A table is confirmed only once it's balanced. Otherwise your seat moves to the next night or comes back as a credit.
Every attendee is ID-verified and 18+. Dinners happen at partner restaurants, and you can report anyone after the night.
Everyone orders and pays for their own meal at the restaurant. The subscription covers matching and the reservation.
No. This page checks whether enough people want it. Leave your email and you will hear when it is ready. Nothing is charged.

demand.summary: Dinners with strangers are a proven paid habit: Timeleft reports €18M ARR and 150k participants a month, but it's positioned as friendship. Attendees say they joined because they were tired of dating apps, and in-person singles events sell out, with women's tickets often selling out first. That points to a singles-only format that guarantees balanced tables.
demand.wtp: Timeleft: about $16 per dinner and $26 per month unlimited (Alta, 2025). Up to $86 per month for subscriptions (News Tribune, 2024). €19.99 per month in Paris (Le Bonbon). €18M ARR and 150,000 monthly participants by August 2025 (Timeleft's CEO, via How They Build).

demand.competitors: Timeleft (dinners with strangers, positioned as friendship, plus women-only tables), local speed-dating organizers on Meetup and Eventbrite, the 222 and Pie apps (in-person social events, snippet only), and singles mixers.
demand.risks: Keeping tables gender-balanced: men's tickets tend to sell more slowly, so this may need men's waitlists or a price difference. It only works in dense cities. Timeleft could easily add a singles mode. Restaurant partnerships and no-shows need deposits or credits. Safety and moderation at in-person events.

name: Reptoll
need: How do I stop scrolling without forcing myself to quit cold turkey?
headline: Pay for your scroll time in push-ups, not willpower.
buyer: People in their 20s and 30s who doomscroll Instagram or TikTok and also want to get fitter
bullets: Your distracting apps stay locked until you earn minutes, with 1 rep buying 1 minute (you set the rate)
The phone camera counts push-ups, squats and planks, so reps have to be real
An emergency pass covers times you can't work out, like when you're at the mall
priceNote: Priced at the low end of the category: Fit to Scroll charges $2.99/mo or $19.99/yr, PushLock $9.99/mo or $39.99/yr. One PushLock reviewer called $39.99 'insane'.

headline: Keep the parts of social media you use. Lose the endless feed.
buyer: Students and professionals who can't delete social apps (for DMs, groups, posting for work) but lose hours to Reels, Shorts and suggested posts
bullets: Opens Instagram, YouTube, Facebook and X with no feed, Reels, Shorts or suggested posts. DMs, search and your own profile still work
Per-site switches set once and sync across your devices and browser profiles

name: Thumbtask

headline: Your to-do list lives in WhatsApp, where you already are.
buyer: Busy people juggling several jobs or side projects who live in WhatsApp or Telegram and abandon task apps after a week

name: Straight-to-Desk
need: How do I get a real person to look at my application instead of it vanishing into the pile?
headline: Skip the stack of 2,000 applications. Send one good note to the person who would actually manage you.
buyer: Job seekers who apply online, never hear back, and want a careful, low-volume way to reach a human.
bullets: Paste a job link. It identifies the likely hiring manager (or a team member who can pass your note along) and their work email

faq.a: Put the phone down, make sure your child is safe, and step away. In the US you can call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) at any time, or call 911 in an emergency. Please talk to a doctor or a qualified professional too.

faq.a: The reset takes 90 seconds. Setting up your flashpoints takes about 3 minutes, and after that it's one tap a day to log a calm day or a tough day.
